text:
### Observed differences

- Activity A01 is completely absent in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces) but runs in about 46 in 100 traces in the later window (92 of 200), with about 191 executions in total — roughly two per trace that contains it — and it sits in the early-to-middle part of the case (median relative position about 0.38). [OCC001, POS001]
- In the later window A01 is wired into the flow: about 53 in 100 of its outgoing transitions go to A05 and about 47 in 100 to A10; in the earlier window A01 had no observed outgoing transitions because it never occurred. [DIR001]
- New transitions into A01 appear from four sides: A05, which previously led only to A10, now leads to A01 in about 47 in 100 of its transitions; A06, previously only to A05, now leads to A01 in about 48 in 100; A03 now leads to A01 in about 35 in 100, mostly at the expense of A03→A05 (about 51 down to 16 in 100); A11 now leads to A01 in about 24 in 100. [DIR003, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- A01's relations change from never co-occurring with anything to being embedded: in the later window it appears together with A02, A04, A05, A09 and A10 in about 46 in 100 traces each, and with A03, A06, A07, A08 and A11 in about 22–33 in 100; it now always co-occurs with A05, A09 and A10, a group that ran in about 53 in 100 traces before and about 46 in 100 after. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL008, REL009, REL010, OCC004, OCC008, OCC009]
- Later activities are pushed about one event position further from earlier ones: A06→A02 moves from lag 4 (about 76 in 100 observed pairs) to lag 5 (about 61 in 100); A03→A02 from lags 4–5 to lag 5 (about 83 in 100); A02→A09 from lags 4–5 to lag 5 only; A05→A10 from lag 1 (about 56 in 100) to lags 1–2; A10→A07 from roughly 42/58 across lags 3–4 to about 79 in 100 at lag 4. The mean event positions of A05, A06, A09 and A10 also shift slightly later (by roughly 0.02–0.04 of a trace). [LAG006, LAG009, LAG021, LAG023, LAG037, POS005, POS006, POS009, POS010]
- Smaller shifts: A03 and A11 each appear in about 32 in 100 traces before and about 28 in 100 after; A02 repeats slightly less often (recurrence in about 53 down to 46 in 100 of its traces); A02 precedes A04 somewhat more often (about 47 up to 54 in 100). [OCC002, OCC003, OCC010, REL012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a new, repeated activity A01 was added into the middle of the process in the later window: it runs in about 46 in 100 cases (about twice per affected case), is entered from A03, A05, A06 or A11, and leads back to A05 or A10, so it sits as a repeatable step inside the A05/A09/A10 part of the flow; its insertion pushes later activities about one event position further from earlier ones. This is shown directly rather than inferred: A01 goes from 0 to 92 of 200 traces, new transitions into and out of A01 appear where none were observed before, co-occurrences with every other activity appear from zero, and more than twenty lag comparisons shift consistently by about one step. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL001, REL004, LAG009, LAG021, LAG023]

Limitations: the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows simply captured different case mixes (for example, A01-type cases absent from the earlier sample) rather than a modified process, and the slight drop in the A05/A09/A10 group's participation (about 53 to 46 in 100) may be sampling variation; the many agreeing occurrence, relation and lag items largely reflect this single insertion and are not independent confirmations. [OCC004, OCC008, OCC009, REL004]

Other differences: A03 and A11 participate slightly less often (about 32 to 28 in 100 traces), A02 recurs slightly less often, and A02 precedes A04 slightly more often (about 47 to 54 in 100); these small shifts could belong to the same insertion or to sampling noise. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC010, REL012]
